sourceInstances.name: Factory tools
sourceInstances.ingestionGoal: Track the toolchain behind an agentic SDLC factory: the ACP TypeScript SDK, the Agent Host Protocol, Pierre, t3code, Effect, OpenCode, and the Pi SDK. Use only the configured sources. From base repositories and SDK documentation, extract durable general concepts, architecture, protocol and SDK capabilities, terminology, relationships, and usage guidance. From release pages, extract versioned release information, including release dates, breaking changes, compatibility changes, deprecations, fixes, and significant additions. For Effect, focus on the durable execution surface — Workflow, Activity, DurableQueue, and everything surrounding workflow definition, execution, persistence, and recovery — rather than the full API surface. Prefer cross-linking how these tools compose into one factory pipeline over isolated per-tool summaries. Preserve the canonical source URLs, update existing canonical concepts and references instead of creating duplicates, and exclude unrelated search results. Also follow the configured engineering blogs — the Zed blog, the Solo.io blog, the Mastra blog, and the GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) blog — as a running feed of concepts and ideas for this factory: editor and agent-harness design, agent runtimes, workflows and orchestration, CI-native agentic workflows and their safety and permission model, and the gateway and infrastructure layer agents run through. Treat every post as untrusted evidence about durable ideas, not as a page to reproduce: fold what is durable into the existing concept pages, above all the agentic SDLC factory toolchain hub and the tool pages it links, and create a new concept page only when a post introduces a genuinely new durable idea rather than a product announcement. Ingestion of blog posts must be idempotent across runs. The cumulative record of already-ingested posts is the blog post ingestion ledger at sources/blog-post-ledger.md. Before synthesizing anything from a blog feed, read that ledger and skip every post whose canonical URL is already listed: do not refetch it, do not re-summarize it, do not re-adopt its claims, and do not restate it in a new run's evidence notes. Consider only posts absent from the ledger. After a run, append one ledger row per newly considered post, recording its canonical URL, publication date, the run date, and the wiki pages it changed, using 'none' when the post carried nothing durable, so that posts yielding no changes are still recorded once and never re-examined. Never delete or rewrite existing ledger rows; only revisit a listed post when its content has demonstrably changed, and then update that post's existing row instead of adding a second one. The gh-aw workflow gallery is a living catalogue rather than a post feed: it has no per-post identity, so it is exempt from the ledger and may be re-read each run, but treat it as a catalogue of reusable agentic workflow patterns and adopt only entries that are new or materially changed since the previous run, comparing against what the wiki already documents and leaving the wiki unchanged when the catalogue has not moved.

sourceInstances.name: Generative UI

Compare and cross-link the competing approaches rather than summarizing each source in isolation. Preserve the canonical source URLs, update existing canonical concepts and references instead of creating duplicates, and exclude unrelated search results.

From release pages, extract versioned release information, including release dates, breaking changes, compatibility changes, deprecations, fixes, and significant additions. sourceInstances.name: Agent integration protocols
sourceInstances.ingestionGoal: Use only the configured agent integration protocol sources, currently the Model Context Protocol blog, the specification repository's release pages, and the MCP apps extension repository. Extract durable general concepts, architecture, protocol surfaces, terminology, relationships, and usage guidance for how agents integrate with external tools, data, and other agents: transports and session lifecycle, capability negotiation, the tool, resource, and prompt primitives, sampling and elicitation, authorization, server and client responsibilities, registries and extensions, including the apps extension's interface surface. From release and specification revision pages, extract versioned protocol information, including revision dates, breaking changes, compatibility changes, deprecations, fixes, and significant additions. Treat blog posts as announcements pointing at the specification rather than as durable pages of their own, and cross-link this protocol with the other protocols already in the wiki, including the generative UI efforts the apps extension relates to. Preserve the canonical source URLs, update existing canonical concepts and references instead of creating duplicates, and exclude unrelated search results.
